<div class="resource-page-main" figma-id="167:238">

<div class="section-blog-hero" figma-id="167:239">

Supply Chain Risk Management

</div>

<div class="blog-heading-wrapper" figma-id="167:245">

# Why CISOs Struggle With Shadow Assets (and What to Do About It)

</div>

<div class="bolg-subtitle" figma-id="167:247">

Why forgotten domains, APIs, cloud services and vendor connections escape inventories, and how continuous discovery reduces the gap.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="blog-hero-right" figma-id="167:261">

<img src="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67e297e4ae74f1e78c32655e/68dd53e8d9ab2b51a5c88178_Why%20CISOs%20Struggle%20With%20Shadow%20Assets_Blog%20(1).png" class="blog-hero-image" data-figma-image-id="6818beb878aa2045faf416d7" sizes="100vw" data-figma-id="167:262" data-figma-image-hash="5b74938b4a59588af6e914d81b8057f2" loading="lazy" srcset="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67e297e4ae74f1e78c32655e/68dd53e8d9ab2b51a5c88178_Why%20CISOs%20Struggle%20With%20Shadow%20Assets_Blog%20(1)-p-500.png 500w, https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67e297e4ae74f1e78c32655e/68dd53e8d9ab2b51a5c88178_Why%20CISOs%20Struggle%20With%20Shadow%20Assets_Blog%20(1)-p-800.png 800w, https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67e297e4ae74f1e78c32655e/68dd53e8d9ab2b51a5c88178_Why%20CISOs%20Struggle%20With%20Shadow%20Assets_Blog%20(1)-p-1080.png 1080w, https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67e297e4ae74f1e78c32655e/68dd53e8d9ab2b51a5c88178_Why%20CISOs%20Struggle%20With%20Shadow%20Assets_Blog%20(1).png 1280w" alt="Unknown domains, APIs, cloud services and supplier connections creating shadow asset risk for CISOs" /><img src="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67dd34931de3a405ce82e3de/683f325456cb7a62a6e6be20_0eb37be808f81aeb4911a08ea034ccd2_blog-hero-Revolutionizes.png" class="blog-hero-image placeholder w-condition-invisible" data-figma-image-id="6818beb878aa2045faf416d7" data-figma-id="167:262" data-figma-image-hash="5b74938b4a59588af6e914d81b8057f2" loading="lazy" alt="ThingsRecon company logo with stylized wing icon on a dark blue background." />

</div>

</div>

<div class="blog-information" figma-id="167:249">

<a href="/authors/sabrina-pagnotta" class="w-inline-block"></a>

<div class="blog-author" figma-id="167:250">

<div class="blog-author-content" figma-id="167:251">

<div class="blog-author-left" figma-id="167:252">

<img src="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67e297e4ae74f1e78c32655e/68c06935808205b1e6c2e123_Profile%20Image%20-%20Sabrina.png" class="image-3" data-figma-image-id="6818beb61992fa71ded39fb2" sizes="100vw" data-figma-id="167:253" data-figma-image-hash="cb48c45c0ed9c2203e505f075ce410de" loading="lazy" srcset="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67e297e4ae74f1e78c32655e/68c06935808205b1e6c2e123_Profile%20Image%20-%20Sabrina-p-500.png 500w, https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67e297e4ae74f1e78c32655e/68c06935808205b1e6c2e123_Profile%20Image%20-%20Sabrina.png 501w" />

</div>

<div class="blog-author-right" figma-id="167:256">

Sabrina Pagnotta

Cybersecurity Writer

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="blog-published-date" figma-id="167:259">

October 1, 2025

July 29, 2026

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="section-blog-body" figma-id="167:263">

<div class="blog-elements-wraper" figma-id="167:264">

<div class="blog-content-wraper" figma-id="167:265">

<div class="div-block-67">

<div class="w-richtext">

Shadow assets persist because cloud, SaaS and supplier change outpace inventories. Outside-in discovery helps CISOs uncover unknown exposure, identify ownership and prioritize assets by business relevance.

</div>

<div class="divider">

</div>

</div>

<div class="blog-content w-richtext">

Every security leader has had that moment: a vulnerability alert tied to a server nobody remembers spinning up, or a SaaS tool paid for on a credit card that suddenly requests access to company data. These aren’t exotic zero-days, they’re everyday shadow assets and forgotten integrations. They create blind spots that don’t show up in inventories, but attackers are scanning for them constantly.

### Where the Gaps Hide

Think of your attack surface as a city map. You know the main streets: your core apps, primary domains, and sanctioned SaaS tools. But between those streets lie alleyways: abandoned subdomains, forgotten APIs, vendor connections you didn’t realize were still active.

Those alleyways are where attackers roam first, because nobody’s watching them. And the bigger your digital ecosystem grows, the more of these blind spots appear. Shadow assets are the default byproduct of modern IT, and we can categorize them into the broad groups:

- **Shadow IT**: Business units spinning up their own SaaS tools and rarely involving security, as it’s perceived as a blocker.

<!-- -->

- **Orphaned Assets**: Past projects leave subdomains, APIs, or cloud instances online long after the team has moved on.

<!-- -->

- **Third-Party Links**: Vendors exposing you indirectly via endpoints or misconfigured systems that still point back to you.

Even in highly regulated sectors like finance, CISOs report these risks in their own 10-Ks — acknowledging that unknown assets and supply chain exposures remain residual risks. They’re typically not flagged in vulnerability scans, because the scanner doesn’t even know where to look. Meanwhile, attackers are running internet-scale discovery against your environment 24/7.

### What CISOs Need Instead

Controls are in place, but blind spots persist. What changes the game isn’t “more scanning,” but **continuous discovery tied to context**:

- Real-time inventory of every internet-facing asset.

<!-- -->

- Automated detection of new exposures the moment they appear.

<!-- -->

- Prioritization that maps technical risk to business impact.

This isn’t about “finding everything”, because that’s a myth. It’s about ensuring that **nothing critical is overlooked**, and that what you do find is ranked by how much it matters.

Key questions to ask yourself:

1.  How up to date is my asset inventory right now, this minute?

<!-- -->

2.  How long does it take me to identify and assign ownership of a new subdomain?

<!-- -->

3.  If a business unit spun up a new SaaS tool yesterday, would I know about it today?

<!-- -->

4.  Am I discovering third-party exposures in real time, or only after a vendor breach hits the news?

The outcome that matters is the confidence that when you brief the board, regulators, or the CEO, you can say with certainty: *“We know what’s out there, and we know what matters most.”*

‍

</div>

</div>
